about: feat-platform-10: the one description of every action form's fields, read by the browser (actionforms.js imports it) and by the dashboard's server (core::drive embeds it), so a step Claude sends and a click Kenny makes are checked against the same words. {stack}, {expect}, {label} and {text} are filled in by both sides the same way. show_when: a field is on screen, checked and sent only while another field has that value ('says' is when, in words); change_when: its label, help and required while another field has that value.

intro.deploy: Creates the container if it does not exist yet, or brings an existing one in line with these files: what the files declare is applied, what they no longer declare is removed from the container. The stack's own data is never touched by this.
intro.deploy-commit: Deploys the stack's files exactly as they were at the chosen earlier commit — the same as Deploy, but from that older version of the working copy instead of today's.
intro.backup: Takes a restic snapshot of the stack's data right now, on top of its nightly backup.
intro.restore: A restore brings the chosen app's data back to the picked snapshot. A safety copy of the current data is kept first, unless "Skip the safety copy" below is ticked.
intro.restore-native: A restore brings this service's data back to the picked snapshot. A safety copy of the current data is always kept first, before anything is overwritten.
intro.update: Pulls the newest image for one app (or every app, left empty) and recreates its container. If the new container does not come up healthy, the previous image is put back automatically.
intro.resize: Applies the memory, CPU core and disk sizes from the manifest to the container that is already running, without recreating it.
intro.enable: Takes the stack back into the nightly backup and update round, and marks it to start automatically when the host boots.
intro.disable: Parks the stack: it is skipped by the nightly backup and update round and no longer starts on boot. The running container itself is not stopped.
intro.adopt:
A "native service" is one program run directly by systemd in the container — no docker. (A docker app is never adopted this way: it comes under management through its docker-compose.yml with a normal Deploy instead.) Adopt takes an already running, hand-built native service on an existing container under management, based on its service.yml.
- checks the manifest and refuses a no-touch guest
- checks the systemd unit is active (this never starts or restarts anything)
- checks the paths the manifest names actually exist
- tags the container as managed and records its unit and binary
- seals its env file into the host's vault
- records the stack in the host's own state
After this, nightly backups, updates by its own policy, and rollback all apply to it the same as any other managed service.
intro.backup-native: Takes a restic snapshot of this adopted service's data right now, on top of its nightly backup.
intro.update-native: Updates this adopted service the way its own manifest's update policy says (for example, only on a named day, or only after a manual check passes) — not immediately just because this was pressed.
intro.release-update-native: Downloads and installs the newest signed release of every native service this stack declares — the same install pipeline Install (one service) uses, run for all of them.
intro.rollback-native: Puts the previous binary this unit was running back in place (the one Install always kept a copy of), and parks the stack's own updates until turned back on.
intro.guards: Applies the runaway guards to this container: caps on how much it may log, limits on journald's own disk use, logrotate, and a weekly cleanup. These are all protective settings — nothing here restarts the container or touches its data.
intro.prune-orphans: Removes files on the container that the working copy's files no longer declare, without running a full deploy — a cleanup for drift that built up outside a deploy.
intro.destroy: Backs up the stack's data, then deletes the container entirely. When the stack's own files are already gone from the working copy, it goes from the host's own record of what it last deployed instead.
intro.forget: For a container that is already gone (deleted outside this dashboard): drops its record from the host's own state and registrations, without touching anything that might still exist.
intro.wipe: Deletes what a retired stack left behind: its backups, its /appdata directory, and any copies kept in the vault. Left empty, Confirm only lists what a real wipe would delete — nothing is deleted until the stack's name is typed below.
intro.patch: Runs `apt update && apt dist-upgrade` on every managed container, one at a time — routine OS patching for the whole fleet.
intro.zfs-replicate: Runs the declared ZFS snapshot and replication jobs right now, instead of waiting for their own schedule.
intro.backup-host-meta: Takes a snapshot of the host daemon's own state right now: its vault, its state file, its TLS material and the intent repository — not any managed stack's data.
intro.backup-devices: Reads and backs up the configuration of every device declared in host.toml (for example, the router) right now.
intro.exec: Runs one shell command inside the named container (`pct exec`), logged on the host for later audit. The host refuses this entirely unless `exec_enabled = true` is set in its own host.toml.
intro.guards-ct: Applies the same runaway guards as Guards (log caps, journald limits, logrotate, weekly cleanup) to any container by its number, including one this working copy does not manage.
intro.template-build: Bakes a fresh golden container template from the chosen OS template (or the host's own default): installs the agent, unattended-upgrades and the orchestrator's own baseline, then stops it ready for cloning. The running fleet is untouched.
intro.update-host: Downloads the chosen (or newest) signed release of the host daemon itself, verifies its checksum, and restarts the host service to run it. The dashboard's own connection drops for a moment while that happens.
intro.answer-check: Records a person's own answer (ok, not ok, or a timed acceptance) to one manual check the fleet check cannot verify by itself.
intro.install-native: Downloads the chosen (or newest) signed release of this native service, verifies it, installs its binary and unit file, then runs Adopt so the host starts managing it the same way as any other adopted service.
intro.apply: Compares the whole stacks directory against the host and applies every difference in one batch: deploys what changed, and destroys only the stacks explicitly typed below to confirm — nothing is destroyed just because it is no longer in the working copy.
intro.restart-host: Restarts the homelab-host.service daemon itself, so a host.toml change that needs a restart takes effect without a full host update.
intro.change-secret: Writes one new value for the named secret straight through latch into the stack's sealed env file. The value itself is never logged or kept in the job's own history.

skip_backup.help: Without it the container's data is backed up first.

skip_safety_copy.label: Skip the safety copy of the current data
skip_safety_copy.help: Without it the data as it is now is kept aside before the restore.

commit.label: Commit

vmid.label: Container number

command.label: Command
command.help: One line, run as root inside the container; the host writes it to its audit log (secrets in it are masked by shape only).

tag.label: Release tag
tag.help: The GitHub releases of this repository, newest first; an unsigned one (no SHA256SUMS.minisig yet) is listed but cannot be chosen.

help_for.install-native: The service's release to install, from its own repository's releases; an unsigned one cannot be chosen.

version.label: Template version
version.help: The number after -homelab-v in the template's name: the next one, e.g. 5 when v4 is the newest.

privileged.label: Privileged template
privileged.help: The second template, for the stacks that must stay privileged (CT 105 and 106); a clone cannot change it.

base.label: Base OS
base.help: The OS template to bake, from the host's list; empty: the host's default.

check.label: Check
check.help: The manual check to answer, from the checks page.

verdict.label: Answer
verdict.help: ok, not ok, or not ok accepted for a number of days (then the days and the reason are asked).

choices.label: not ok, accepted for some days

days.label: Number of days
days.help: How many days this not ok counts as accepted, 1 to 3650.

show_when.says: the answer is "not ok, accepted for some days"

change_when.label: Reason
change_when.help: Required with this answer: one line on why this not ok is accepted.

destroy.label: Destroy these gone stacks
destroy.help: The plan lists the stacks whose directory is gone. Type the name of each one to destroy, comma-separated; empty: nothing is destroyed.

messages.typed_wrong: That is not {expect}; type the stack's name exactly.

edit.about: feat-platform-10: the edit forms (stack settings, the raw editor, add an app, the firewall and its rule dialog, the plan dialog's commit step, the new-stack wizard, a host.toml key, the batch and roll back dialogs), described once. editforms.js draws them from here and core::driveedit checks a driven step against the same words. {label}, {lower}, {min}, {max}, {expect}, {text}, {stack}, {key}, {name}, {vmid}, {peer}, {part} are filled in the same way on both sides.

messages.number: {label} must be a whole number from {min} to {max}.
messages.subject: A commit needs a subject.
messages.raw_unchanged: The file is as it was.
messages.name_taken: There is a stack called {name} already.
messages.peer_form: {peer} is not an address like 10.10.10.4 or a network like 10.10.10.0/24.
messages.peer_host_bits: {peer} has host bits set: Proxmox reads it as the whole network. Write one address, or the network.
messages.icmp_ports: icmp has no ports; clear them.
messages.port_proto: A port needs tcp or udp.
messages.port_range: {part} is not a port 1 to 65535 or a forward range.
messages.key_window: A number and a unit, e.g. 24h.
messages.rollback_choose: Choose a commit to deploy or a unit to roll back.
messages.tile_down_low: {key}: down after ({down} s) must be at least check every ({watch} s).
messages.retention_json: A JSON list of {"every_days": N, "span_days": N} (span_days optional).
messages.retention_not_json: Not valid JSON: a list like [] or [{"every_days": 1, "span_days": 7}].
messages.dollar_expand: must not contain '${': latch --expand parses every file it is given, so one unresolvable placeholder would break every stack's secrets, not only this one's.
